searchText: <@577788234810130432> whats the reasoning for building on Prague + Frames instead of bogota-devnet-2? I think this is a leftover of the original PoC of this devnet I agree that what we need is something on top of bogota-devnet-2 But I think we will keep devnets separated: Daisugi for experimenting aggregation, and whatever we do on top of bogota is done starting with no aggregation This is my understanding, could be wrong, but I think it's the best whati s the difference between these 2 networks ? Daisugi currently misses some of the latest bogota (Hegota devnet on the EL side) features That’s why at the beginning of this thread I suggested that we spec something for Daisugi on top of bogota-devnet-2 specs meant between Prague + Frames vs bogota-devnet-2? What I mean is: - Daisugi adds features on top of some base branch - This base branch currently isn't `bogota-devnet-2` (the most Hegota up-to-date EL branch out there) but a Nethermind-specific branch which implements just EIP-8141, EIP-7906, EIP-8250, and some form of EIP-8288. - This isn't a common ground for all ELs, and now that we want more clients to easily join, we need this common ground. It'd be better to base Daisugi features (mostly 8288 work) on top of a common ground for EL clients, i.e., `bogota-devnet-2`. - Otherwise, we'll need to maintain a separate branch with just the features I mentioned above. - Clients will still need to maintain a branch for Daisugi, but we can reuse the branch that we are all agreeing on today as a base and upgrade it as Bogota devnets upgrade. Oh, I now understand Justin's question. Daisugi isn't built on top of Fusaka nor Glamsterdam. I didn't notice that before I now have the same question (I still think that we need to rebase Daisugi on top of `bogota-devnet-2`)

excerpts.author: ivanlitteri
excerpts.content:
What I mean is:
- Daisugi adds features on top of some base branch
- This base branch currently isn't `bogota-devnet-2` (the most Hegota up-to-date EL branch out there) but a Nethermind-specific branch which implements just EIP-8141, EIP-7906, EIP-8250, and some form of EIP-8288. 
- This isn't a common ground for all ELs, and now that we want more clients to easily join, we need this common ground. It'd be better to base Daisugi features (mostly 8288 work) on top of a common ground for EL clients, i.e., `bogota-devnet-2`.
- Otherwise, we'll need to maintain a separate branch with just the features I mentioned above.
- Clients will still need to maintain a branch for Daisugi, but we can reuse the branch that we are all agreeing on today as a base and upgrade it as Bogota devnets upgrade.
